scope_note: Authoritative family-recognition backfill centered on the canonical local Diospyros texana learner, with Diospyros virginiana retained as a family/species comparison pending the project's strict target-zone review.

actions: Restored Ericales / Ebenaceae to Diospyros texana and Diospyros virginiana in the Master Plant Pool.
Preserved Diospyros texana as the canonical local anchor.
Flagged Diospyros virginiana as Texas-native but still pending the project's 3-exact-target-county range review; Texas A&M describes Travis County as the western edge of its natural habitat.
Recorded the conflict between broader FNA/USFS/Texas A&M descriptions of D. texana as dioecious and the UT Williamson treatment reporting monoecious material.

family_lesson.where_to_look_first: Start with a woody plant bearing alternate simple entire leaves and small axillary urn/bell-shaped flowers. The strongest family confirmation is the fleshy berry sitting in a conspicuous persistent, often enlarged calyx.
family_lesson.strongest_field_confirmation: Woody tree/shrub + alternate exstipulate entire leaves + fused urn/campanulate corolla + mostly unisexual flowers + superior multi-loculed ovary + fleshy berry with an enlarged persistent calyx.
core_characters: Trees or shrubs with very dense, hard wood.
Leaves alternate, simple, usually entire and without stipules.
Terminal buds absent in the FNA Diospyros framework.
Flowers usually unisexual; staminate flowers often in small cymes and pistillate flowers commonly solitary.
Calyx persistent and often accrescent/enlarged in fruit.
Corolla fused, urn-shaped to bell-shaped, with overlapping/twisted lobes in bud.
Staminate flowers often have numerous stamens rather than just 4–5.
Ovary superior and multi-loculed with 1–2 ovules per locule.
Fruit a fleshy berry with several large hard seeds.
avoid_overgeneralizing: Do not teach the family as always dioecious: Diospyros is usually dioecious, but local-source treatments disagree on the sex system of D. texana.
Do not identify persimmons by fruit color alone; local species differ strongly in bark, leaves, fruit size, pubescence and calyx/flower anatomy.
Do not confuse the persistent calyx with a separate leaf-like fruit structure; it is the flower calyx retained and enlarged beneath the berry.
Do not call every dark-fruited persimmon D. texana without checking leaf size/pubescence and bark.
Do not promote D. virginiana to strict project-native status until the 3-target-county rule is independently satisfied.

fastest_cues: Smooth pale gray bark that exfoliates in patches to reveal white, gray and pink tones.
Tiny thick leaves, about 2–5 cm, rounded to notched at the tip.
Flowers on twigs of the previous season.
Five sepals and five corolla lobes.
Black, small, hairy berry about 1.5–2.5 cm.
Fruit usually contains several triangular/light-red to glossy-brown seeds.
high_value_micromorphology: Staminate anthers dehisce by short subapical slits.
Pistillate flowers lack staminodes in FNA/UT treatments.
Ovary and mature berry are pubescent.

Diospyros virginiana.role: family comparison; strict target-zone review pending
fastest_cues: Dark reddish-brown to gray bark divided into deep square/blocky 'alligator' plates.
Much larger leaves, usually 6–15 cm, with pointed acute/acuminate tips.
Leaf undersides mostly glabrous or only sparsely hairy.
Four sepals and four corolla lobes.
Yellow-orange to dark red fruit, usually much larger at about 3–5 cm.
Fruit mostly glabrous and holds several large reddish-brown seeds.
high_value_micromorphology: Staminate anthers open along their full length.
Pistillate flowers usually carry about 8 staminodes.

fast_key: Smooth mottled exfoliating pale bark + tiny rounded leaves + small black hairy berry -> Diospyros texana.
Dark deeply blocky alligator bark + large pointed leaves + large orange/yellow fruit -> Diospyros virginiana.
Fleshy fruit with huge persistent 4–5-lobed calyx + alternate entire leaves -> strongly supports Diospyros/Ebenaceae.
Milky latex + thorny twigs + a few large glossy seeds -> reconsider Sapotaceae/Sideroxylon.
Small red drupe with several hard pyrenes and tiny axillary flowers -> reconsider Aquifoliaceae/Ilex.

evidence: Flora of North America describes Diospyros generally as usually dioecious and broader species references/US Forest Service/Texas A&M describe D. texana as dioecious.
UT Austin's detailed Williamson County treatment explicitly labels D. texana monoecious and describes 1–3 staminate flowers plus solitary pistillate flowers on the same plant.
sex_system_note.learner_rule: Teach staminate versus pistillate flower anatomy, but do not use plant-level sex system alone to identify D. texana until this discrepancy is reconciled.

Diospyros texana.staminate: Usually smaller/clustered flowers; 5-part flower, commonly about 16 stamens; anthers open by short subapical slits.
Diospyros texana.pistillate: Usually solitary; 5-lobed persistent calyx; white urn-shaped 5-lobed corolla; superior 4-chambered hairy ovary; no staminodes in FNA/UT treatments.

Diospyros virginiana.staminate: Usually clustered 2–3-flowered cymes; 4-part corolla; about 16 stamens; anthers open along their full length.
Diospyros virginiana.pistillate: Usually solitary; 4-part persistent calyx/corolla; superior ovary; typically about 8 staminodes; four styles united basally.

fruit_lesson.family_key: The persistent calyx remains attached at the fruit base and often enlarges substantially, making the berry look as if it is sitting on a leafy saucer.
fruit_lesson.Diospyros texana: Small black pubescent berry, commonly 3–8 seeded; pulp darkens black and strongly stains.
fruit_lesson.Diospyros virginiana: Larger yellow-orange to reddish berry, usually glabrous; multiple large reddish-brown seeds; persistent calyx is very conspicuous.
visual_sequence: young fruit with same calyx retained
fruit cut open to show multiple seeds

bark_lesson.Diospyros texana: Smooth, thin, mottled/exfoliating bark in pale gray-white-pink tones; one of the fastest Central Texas field characters even without fruit.
bark_lesson.Diospyros virginiana: Dark bark deeply furrowed into blocky square plates — classic 'alligator bark'.
bark_lesson.teaching_value: Bark gives an excellent winter/sterile comparison and is much safer than relying on fruit color.

Sapotaceae.confusion: Woody plants with alternate entire leaves, small flowers and fleshy fruit.
Sapotaceae.tie_breaker: Local Sideroxylon commonly has milky latex, thorny short shoots and fruit with a few large glossy seeds; Diospyros lacks the latex/thorn combination and has the huge persistent calyx.

Aquifoliaceae.confusion: Alternate simple leaves, unisexual flowers and fleshy fruit.
Aquifoliaceae.tie_breaker: Ilex fruits are smaller drupes with several pyrenes and usually a small persistent stigma; Diospyros fruit is a true berry with several large seeds and a conspicuous enlarged persistent calyx.
